characterList.name: Aaron

characterList.description: Man with short dark hair and beard, wearing a white T-shirt with 'Bernie' printed on it. Sits in the middle of an orange sofa, holding a microphone and a notepad.
characterList.name: Michael

characterList.description: Man with short reddish hair and glasses, wearing a brown suit and a blue tie. Reclines on the right side of the orange sofa.
characterList.name: Thomas

content_metadata.description: A satirical interview with Thomas Wellington from Activate, a fictional youth political organization, discussing their controversial stance on supporting Jacob Rees-Mogg for leadership.

activities.description: Aaron, Michael, and Thomas engage in an interview

characterInteraction.description: Collaborate to interrogate Thomas, showing skepticism and incredulity.
Attempts to maintain composure while deflecting criticism and promoting Activate's agenda.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Activate's alignment with figures like Trump and Rees-Mogg suggests an affinity for nationalist and socially conservative ideologies.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Emphasized by a Star Wipe effect and upbeat music, highlighting the absurdity of Activate's position.

narrativeProgression.description: Interviewers introduce Thomas Wellington from Activate.
Questioning about the recent split within Activate over Jacob Rees-Mogg's endorsement.
Probing Activate's values, highlighting their controversial support for Rees-Mogg.
Challenge on the practicality of Activate's ambition to make Rees-Mogg Prime Minister.
Thomas asserts independence from the Conservative Party and commitment to lobbying for Rees-Mogg.
Directing viewers to Activate's Twitter page for more information.
Interview concludes with thanks to Thomas.

scenes.thematicElements: Political activism and youth engagement, populism rise, influence of online platforms, tension between traditional values and contemporary political realities.
scenes.title: Interview with Thomas Wellington

videoEditingDetails.description: Black screen with white text reading 'A fine opportunity to observe the spice homo chav. And gas them all.' appears.
Still image of a man in a suit with a top hat with animated streaks behind him and the text 'ACTIVATE MOGG NOW!!!'.

Still image of Jeremy Corbyn raising his hands in celebration with the text 'FOR THE MANY NOT THE FEW' appears on a blue background. Text reading 'IT'S A TRAP' and 'ACTIVATE' appears below with a fictional alien character.
Still image of people gathered in front of 10 Downing Street. Jacob Rees-Mogg is standing in the center of the group.
Still image of a Twitter post with a press release from Activate.
Star Wipe transition with upbeat orchestral music.

climax.description: Thomas explicitly states Activate's intention to break away from the Conservative Party to back Jacob Rees-Mogg for leadership.

youtube_description:
Tonight we interviewed Thomas Wellington, founder of Activate - the Tory answer to Momentum.
Mr Wellington explained how the biggest division within the organisation is whether Theresa May should step down, with the Activate leadership calling on Jacob Rees-Mogg to replace her as both party leader and Prime Minister.

This may be a spoof interview.
---

The UK is facing an economic crisis, falling living standards, a climate crisis, the rise of the far-right. More than ever, we need a resilient Left. This means we need a strong Left media, capable of thinking honestly about the issues facing us, tackling these issues head-on, as well as reaching out to those who aren’t yet on side. Our wide range of output – from listicles to essays, from punchy videos to in-depth discussions – does exactly that.

But all this costs money: studio rent, equipment, contributor fees and digital infrastructure. We do a lot with a little, but we can’t do anything with nothing. We won’t charge for content or cash in on sponsorship deals with Pepsi. We don’t have private fortunes, or state backers, or big capital behind us – we just have you.

Not everyone can afford to give – but if you enjoy our work, and you believe in what we’re doing, maybe you could forego a couple of your preferred beverages this month and lend us a hand instead. In the longer term, growing our regular subscriber base will allow us to meet the future well-prepared – so if you can spare a few quid a month, why not sign up for a regular subscription?

We’ve achieved so much already – but the truth is, we’ve barely begun. Be a part of the change. Help us build a new media for a different politics.
